# glpi_software_license (Resource)

GLPI software license.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glpi_software" "editor" {
  name = "Editor"
}

resource "glpi_software_license_type" "subscription" {
  name = "Subscription"
}

resource "glpi_software_license" "team" {
  name        = "Editor team plan"
  software_id = glpi_software.editor.id
  type_id     = glpi_software_license_type.subscription.id
  number      = 25
  expire      = "2027-12-31"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the item.
- `software_id` (Number) ID of the software.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Free-form comment.
- `entity_id` (Number) ID of the entity that owns the item. 0 is the root entity.
- `expire` (String) Expiration date as YYYY-MM-DD.
- `location_id` (Number) ID of the location.
- `manufacturer_id` (Number) ID of the publisher.
- `number` (Number) Number of installations the license covers. -1 means unlimited.
- `otherserial` (String) Inventory number.
- `purchased_version_id` (Number) ID of the purchased software version.
- `serial` (String) License serial number.
- `state_id` (Number) ID of the status.
- `type_id` (Number) ID of the license type.
- `used_version_id` (Number) ID of the software version in use.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) GLPI numeric ID.
- `valid` (Boolean) Whether the license is valid, computed by GLPI.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by GLPI numeric ID.
terraform import glpi_software_license.example 42
```
